title: SLA-driven synthetic prompt canaries for pinned model swaps
creator: Leah Kim
description: Goal: Provide a first-class, automated canary gating flow for model swaps that are behind customer pins using a curated synthetic prompt suite tied to SLA and quality gates. This ticket scopes the PM and product acceptance criteria for a system that can run deterministic checks on new model revisions before they receive production traffic, and that can continuously A/B the pinned variant with traffic-aware weighting once the canary passes. Motivation: pinned model swaps are high-risk for customers who expect strict latency and availability SLAs. Existing shadow and small-cohort mechanisms exercise production traffic but are noisy and slow to iterate. A synthetic prompt canary gives an early, reproducible view into latency, correctness signal regressions, and token-cost delta while minimizing customer exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Define and publish a canonical synthetic prompt suite format (JSONL) and tooling to produce per-customer weighted prompt subsets

Canary run that evaluates latency P95, token-cost per request, and a lightweight correctness proxy (e.g., intent classification or regression score) on a new pinned revision within a configurable timebox
Automatic pass/fail decision computed against configurable SLO thresholds (latency, cost, correctness) with statistical power checks - gating the rollout when fail
Integration with Console rollouts UI: show canary results, SLO deltas, and a single-click promote/rollback for pinned swaps
When canary passes, lightweight A/B traffic ramp templates published (0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25%) with automated rollback triggers linked to drift and error rate thresholds
Audit trail: every gated pinned swap creates an immutable record (who promoted, what prompt set used, runtime profile, and a link to raw telemetry)
implementation_notes: Synthetic prompt suite should include categories: latency-sensitive short prompts, long-context generation, high-entropy prompts, and adversarial edge cases
Default suite shipped with the platform; customers can supply an override per pin (uploaded JSONL or referencing a Console saved promptset)
Gate evaluation should run on the same serving topology customers use (hosted vs dedicated vs private) to ensure kernel selection and quantization effects are represented
Statistical power requirement: by default target 80% power to detect 10% relative degradation in the correctness proxy; allow tuning by customer
Leverage existing telemetry pipeline (metrics + traces) and add a canary result schema for Console; minimal extra cardinality to avoid ingestion cost blowups
Provide a CLI and SDK hook so solution engineers can run canaries pre-PR and attach results to model onboarding docs
Risk: synthetic prompts can overfit to benchmarks. Mitigation: combine synthetic checks with rapid, low-weight real traffic A/B for a final verification phase
